**Riley Brooks**
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

Date: [Date I am mailing this letter]

Molina Healthcare
Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Member appeal — denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827)**
- **Member:** Riley Brooks
- **Member ID:** W997409334
- **Reference number:** POC-AA9EA32E7D-95281
- **Date of denial notice:** August 9, 2026
- **Plan:** Molina Healthcare, Commercial/ACA, Mississippi
- **Governing policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy — https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, orthopedic surgery. I am asking Molina to reconsider this determination and approve the surgery. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in Molina's hands meet the plan's own published requirements.

The notice dated August 9, 2026 states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. Respectfully, the records do document that trial, and I set it out below next to the plan's own language.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy states:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

The same three-month requirement appears elsewhere in the policy as well:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration, including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My non-surgical treatment lasted longer than three months and included more than one type of treatment:

| The plan's requirement | What my records show |
|---|---|
| Non-surgical management for at least three (3) months | NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; supervised physical therapy for 12 weeks, from April 1, 2026 to June 24, 2026, with 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; corticosteroid injection on May 19, 2026. Taken together, my conservative care spans well beyond three months. |
| Failure of that management | My symptoms have continued for 12 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief. The injection gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. The physical therapy, which focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, was completed and did not resolve my symptoms. |
| "at least two of the following as appropriate" | My records document three distinct non-surgical treatments: supervised physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and a corticosteroid injection. |

The policy also lists, as a criterion:

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

My records show that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. My examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. My MRI of June 16, 2026 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## An important limit on what I have been able to review

The excerpts of MCP-404 that I have been able to obtain introduce lists of further conditions that are not reproduced in the material available to me. Each of the following sentences ends in a colon, and the itemized list that follows it is not something I have in front of me:

> "Diagnostic arthroscopy may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "Arthroscopic debridement (limited or extensive) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

> "Arthroscopic distal clavicle excision and subacromial decompression/acromioplasty may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

Because of that, I cannot confirm which section of the policy Molina applied to CPT 29827, or which specific treatments on the plan's list Molina counted or did not count. I am not able to state a threshold the plan has not published to me, and I have not quoted any requirement beyond the language above. I am asking Molina to identify the exact criteria it used so that I can respond to them directly.

## My written request for the criteria that were applied

The criteria used to decide my case are held by the plan, not by me, and I am requesting them here in writing. Please provide me, in writing:

1. **The guideline title and criteria applied to my determination**, including the specific version used, and, if an MCG guideline was used, the MCG guideline title;
2. The full text of the section of Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy that was applied to CPT 29827, including every item in any list that my excerpts show only as a colon;
3. The name, specialty, and credentials of the reviewer who made this determination; and
4. A statement of which of my documented conservative treatments were counted toward the plan's non-surgical management requirement and which were not, and why.

The plan holds these criteria. I cannot meet a standard I have not been shown, and I am asking Molina to supply it.

## What I am asking Molina to do

Please overturn the denial dated August 9, 2026 (reference POC-AA9EA32E7D-95281) and authorize the rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827, as requested by Dr. Reyes. If the reviewer still intends to uphold the denial, I ask that the decision identify, point by point, which criterion in MCP-404 my records do not satisfy and what specific documentation would satisfy it.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 5, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that window. I am sending this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for my plan. I understand I may also file through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card, and I will confirm the appeal window shown on my denial letter.

Please send all correspondence about this appeal to me at the address above. I am happy to authorize Dr. Reyes's office to speak with Molina about the clinical record, and additional records can be sent on request.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Riley Brooks**
Member ID: W997409334
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-09] · [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-24] · [MRI report, 2026-06-16] · [Office notes from Dr. Reyes] · [Injection record, 2026-05-19] · [Medication history]
